questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Linear Form
questions.problem: The linear form $f(x)$ is defined as $f(x)=ax,$ where $a=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}].$  Evaluate the function when $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Substituting $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =ax \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot 5+2\cdot 2 \\  & =-6-5+4 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the bilinear form $B(x,y),$ given by 

$$
B(x,y)=2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{3}+{x}_{3}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{3}{y}_{2}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
We are given that 

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$ 

Substituting these into the bilinear expression, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-4{x}_{2}{y}_{3}+{x}_{3}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{3}{y}_{2} \\  & =2\cdot (-2)\cdot 0-4\cdot 2\cdot 3+(-1)\cdot 1-3\cdot (-1)\cdot 0 \\  & =0-24-1-0 \\  & =-25.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
B(x,y)={x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}.
$$

 

Evaluate $B(x,y)$ when $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:

$$

questions.knowledge_point: Writing Down a Bilinear Form Given Its Matrix
questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ above. Which of the following represents the corresponding bilinear form ${x}^{T}\,Ay$ in terms of the components of $x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]?$
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

Each entry ${a}_{ij}$ of $A$ corresponds to the term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-3){x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+1{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

**Method 2**

To write down a bilinear form in terms of vector components, we compute the following expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{T}\,Ay & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & \,\,-3 \\ \,\,3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2} \\ 3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{1}(2{y}_{1}-3{y}_{2})+{x}_{2}(3{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}) \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-3{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

$$

The matrix of the bilinear form $B(x,y)=6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}$ is given above. What is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
Each term ${a}_{ij}{x}_{i}{y}_{j}$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry ${a}_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}-2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2} \\  & =6{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+(-2){x}_{1}{y}_{2} \\  & +\,0{x}_{2}{y}_{1}\,+3{x}_{2}{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

$$
[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, $a=-2$ and $b=3.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b=(-2)+3=1.
$$

\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{2}-{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{2}{y}_{3}-{x}_{3}{y}_{1} \\  & =2\cdot 1\cdot 2-1\cdot 2+3\cdot 1\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4-2+3-2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Matrix of a Bilinear Form
canonical_examples.problem:
The matrix of the bilinear form $B(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}) = 2x_1y_1 + 2x_2y_1 - x_3 y_2+2x_3y_3$ is given below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & 0 & 0 \\ b & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & c & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Each term $a_{ij}x_i y_j$ in the expression of the bilinear form corresponds to the entry $a_{ij}$ of the matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}B(x,y) & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}-{x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{1}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,2{x}_{2}{y}_{1}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+0{x}_{2}{y}_{3} \\  & +\,0{x}_{3}{y}_{1}+(-1){x}_{3}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, the corresponding matrix of the bilinear form is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14043646/assets/24b1e29dccdff51c2ca2c7780a8a5dfcf9c74ed91d48afdde8a14c5127f89ce1.png)

Therefore, $a=2,$ $b=2,$ and $c=-1.$ Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=2+2+(-1) = 3.
$$
